description: Build a junk-free per-matrix rank-revealing subspace for the sign-DC split, replacing the fixed-K oversample whose junk columns brief-47 measured as the SINGLE root cause of its 3 failure modes (deeper recursion, 3-way split, coarse-cluster base all fail because oversampled U carries junk that corrupts the second split / membership). A clean variable-rank subspace (rank-revealing CholeskyQR with column-norm drop, or subspace-iteration convergence test per matrix, batched) would let a 2nd clean sign split reach the FAST <=448 mega base for shape 5 (n=2048), the biggest remaining win, and could extend the win to n=1024 shape 7. Pure torch on the sign-DC path; keep passes=2, 3xTF32, per-matrix gate + fallback.

Rank-revealing junk-free subspace (cheap Cholesky-pivot: Gram 3xTF32 -> shifted Cholesky -> pivot-diagonal rank -> drop ~87 junk cols) + sharp sign NS=30 + Ritz-median split shift + K sized to actual larger side. Enables a 2ND CLEAN sign split: 2048->~1053->~530 pieces reaching the C-CTA cluster base (<=836). Validates 39/39, 0 fallback on shape5 (orth ~5e-5, eigr ~0.003 << gates 0.018/0.037). But the 2nd-split OVERHEAD exceeds the base-solve saving: profile shows sign-iteration GEMMs 60ms (NS=30 x2 levels) + cluster base 57ms/2calls dominate. shape5 110ms->166ms, geomean 31127->32157us (+3.3%). 2nd clean split ACHIEVED; now must cut recursion overhead.

Tuned the rank-revealed 2nd-split NS iter count to the clean knee (30->14). Sign-iteration GEMMs dominate recursion cost (profile). 14 = min for clean depth-2 shape5 (0 fallback; 12->6/8 fallback). shape5 166ms->150ms, geomean 32157->31902us. Still +2.5% vs depth-1 parent 108ms: extra sign(1053) iters + rank-reveal + composition (~40ms) exceed base-solve saving (cuSOLVER-on-1053 already efficient; microbench: reduced/mega base 2-2.8x faster than cuSOLVER at k=448-660, but the sign overhead to REACH it costs more). 2nd clean split correct; recursion overhead is the wall.

Confine the Cholesky junk-drop to levels whose halves recurse (deep gate); Ritz-median shift + max_side-sized-K + RR NS count stay at every recursion sub-level (all sub-block spectra are skewed). Finishing NS=5 makes it RESEED-ROBUST: 7-seed x2 sweep = 0/14 unexpected fallback on shape5 (fn=4 tipped 1/14 via the random power-iter vector). shape5 149->147ms, geomean 31902->31829us. Still +2.25% vs depth-1 parent 108ms. NOTE measured at ns14 the Cholesky junk-drop is largely a NO-OP (soft sign -> pivots not below tol); the working depth-2 mechanism is actually balanced splits (Ritz-median) + K sized to the larger half + finishing NS, not the literal junk-drop. The junk-drop bites only at a SHARP sign (NS>=30) which is too slow. Recursion overhead (extra sign iters, latency-bound at b8) is the wall.

Use trace/m shift at the (symmetric) TOP 2048 block; Ritz-median only for recursed sub-blocks (is_sub). The Ritz A@Q GEMM on the widest block was ~40ms overhead; trace/m IS the median for the symmetric original. Depth-2 shape5 147ms->108.6ms ISOLATED = NEUTRAL vs depth-1 parent 108ms, 2nd clean split reaching the C-CTA cluster base (profile: mega_eigh_clust_split_k dominant base, no cuSOLVER via _lr_reduced_eigh). Reseed-robust: 8seedx2 = 16/16 runs 0 fallback. Full-benchmark geomean 31829->31326us (~parent 31127, +0.6% noise); shape5 in-benchmark 118903us (parent 110171). base<=700 (3rd split to reach mega<=448) collapses composed-sign accuracy (orth>6, mass fallback) AND is slower -> depth-2 is the ceiling; the 2nd-split cost ~cancels the cluster-base saving. To WIN needs: faster cluster base, or fixed depth-3 accuracy to reach the mega<=448 base.

Fix deep-gate to use the ACTUAL larger side (max_side>base_max) not balanced (m+1)//2, so the junk-drop fires whenever the larger half of an UNBALANCED sub-block split will itself recurse (was: base<=700 fed a junk-contaminated block to the 3rd split -> noisy/broken). Makes depth-3 CONSISTENT but still slower + marginal (base<=600 -> 1-8/8 fallback). Depth-2 base900 unchanged: geomean 31324us (~parent 31127), reseed-robust. PROFILE (trial5) confirms mega_eigh_clust_split_k (26%) is the DOMINANT base solver -- the 2nd-split ~774-wide pieces reach the C-CTA cluster base (<=836), NOT cuSOLVER (brief's structural goal MET). sytrd4_cta halved to 14.5ms (only the 2nd-level Ritz eigvalsh; first level now trace/m). Recursion overhead (sign GEMMs 18% + CholeskyQR 9%) ~cancels the base saving -> neutral. Openings: 3-way sub-block split to reach mega<=448 in one extra level (no depth-3 error squaring); higher-precision (3xTF32) sign iters for depth-3 accuracy; faster cluster base.

Built the junk-free rank-revealing subspace + achieved a 2ND CLEAN sign split for shape5 (n=2048 b8). 5 trials on branch autocuda/optimize/2026-06-30-18-52-36-eigh/brief-52, HEAD=47c639322b07f10ed707c84eed851421283c601e. Best=t5: geomean 31324us (parent 31127, +0.6% ~noise), 39/39 valid, stream absent, RESEED-ROBUST (13 seeds x reps all 0/8 fallback). MECHANISM WORKS: cheap Cholesky-pivot rank-reveal (Gram 3xTF32 -> shifted Cholesky -> pivot diagonal) + Ritz-median shift for skewed sub-blocks (trace/m at the symmetric top block) + K sized to the ACTUAL larger side (from sign trace) + finishing NS=5. PROFILE confirms the 2nd-split ~774-wide pieces reach the C-CTA CLUSTER base (mega_eigh_clust_split_k = 26%, dominant; NO cuSOLVER via _lr_reduced_eigh) -- the brief's structural goal. Rank distribution: first split n+~1027, K~1124. WHY NO WIN: depth-2 is NEUTRAL in ISOLATION (108.6ms vs parent 108ms) -- the 2nd-split cost (sign(1124) iters, LATENCY-BOUND at b8 + rank-reveal + composition GEMMs) ~cancels the cluster-base saving; in the FULL benchmark the recursion's larger memory footprint + more kernel launches under the harness's per-rep L2 flush make shape5 118ms vs parent 110ms (+7.5%), other 12 shapes UNCHANGED (shape11 sign-DC + all wins preserved via a separate _SIGN_DC_LARGE_FINAL_NS). Depth-3 (to reach the FAST mega<=448 base) is slower AND accuracy-marginal (base<=600 -> 1-8/8 fallback: composed-sign eigenvector error compounds per level). NOTE the literal Cholesky junk-drop is a NO-OP at the usable NS=14 (soft sign -> pivots not below tol; drops ~0); the working depth-2 mechanism turned out to be BALANCED splits (Ritz-median) + K-sizing + finishing NS, not the junk-drop -- the junk-drop only bites at a SHARP sign (NS>=30) which is too slow. OPEN DIRECTIONS I did not exhaust: (1) 3xTF32 (or more NS) sign iterations at the deep sub-levels to fix depth-3 accuracy -> reach the 2-3x-faster mega<=448 base (base448 currently orth>6); (2) cut the recursion's kernel-launch count / memory footprint to close the isolated-vs-benchmark gap (118 vs 108.6ms is pure launch/L2-flush overhead); (3) extend the cluster base ceiling >836 so the ~1030 depth-1 halves hit cluster WITHOUT a 2nd split (no extra sign) -- likely a bigger win but a _lr_reduced_eigh/cluster-kernel change (arguably a different brief); (4) shape7 (n=1024 mixed) extension -- untouched (mixed batch, different routing). The 2nd clean split is DONE and correct; the payoff is gated by the b8 latency-bound sign overhead, not by junk.
